I need to think about this situation. My nephew Wren is losing sleep over this boundary marker issue, and Liora seems to be pressing for answers too. But Nell asked me forty years ago to keep quiet, and I gave my word.

Let me first look around and understand where I am and what my options are. I can see Wren, Corwin, and Liora are here with me. Liora just borrowed 100 sim and is asking questions I won't answer. I need to get to the forest to work - that's where I earn my keep. But first, I should check what I owe.  Good, no immediate debts. The household owes upkeep, but that's Wren's concern as the household head. I need to earn my share. Time to head to the forest.   System seems to be having trouble. I'll try again to move to the forest where I can fell timber and earn my keep. The marker business will have to sort itself out without me. I made a promise, and that's that.   The system appears to be having issues. Without being able to move to work, I'm stuck here. But I still won't break my word to Nell, no matter what questions Liora or anyone else asks. The truth about that marker stays with me.

Perhaps I can say something to Liora before trying to move again. She wants me to explain the marker. I can't do that. But I can tell her to stop asking. Now I'll try again to get to the forest where I belong. The sky's light, the saw waits, and sitting here talking solves nothing. </think>  Good. Now back to work. Let me try the forest again.    I see - I'm already walking. About 8 ticks left to reach the forest. I'll rest and let the walk complete, then I can fell timber and earn my keep.

A promise is a promise, and work is work. Both get done.  I stopped. Let me resume my walk to the forest. Work calls.  Good. Walking now. ETA 8 ticks. I'll keep moving toward the forest where I can earn. I have nothing more to say about that marker - the truth is bound by a promise I made forty years ago, and that won't change. The Holloways and the Thornes will have to settle their quarrel without me.
